New paper: base models can already reason, they just need the right opening line. Fixing a starting token cue like 'Okay' lifts Olmo-3-7B from 42% to 78% on MATH-500, near RL-trained levels. RL didn't install reasoning; it just taught the cues. https://t.co/iiR1VkRcgV

Let a small controller decide who thinks next. S1-MAS uses it for task selection and stopping, leaving reasoning to LLM workers. With GPT-4o-mini workers, a GPT controller used ~4× GPT tokens and had slightly lower mean accuracy across 3 benchmarks. https://t.co/pTazNXb8xz

RL makes LLMs better mostly where they were already good. Noukhovitch, Ivison, Lambert and Courville found that on AIME, RL added 63 pass-rate points on easy problems and 3 on hard ones. They call it the Matthew effect in RL.

https://t.co/1iYJbgFdXz https://t.co/FCVHkrkgDd

Xiaomi's MiMo-V2.6 tech report is a masterclass in scaling RL:

• ~3B tokens per RL step, up to 1M context
• code, visual & cyber environments
• frozen MoE router for stability

RL framework + environments are open-sourced.

https://t.co/ANiZMC34IR

they flipped the rewards, randomized them, even wiped them. improvement curve barely budged. reward's effect was about 14% of just putting the trajectory in context. so much for "in-context rl"

IdeaScientist first tried RL on its whole research pipeline. The base model rarely finished, leaving little learning signal. They switched to training each role separately, then recomposed the agents.

A team still needs learnable jobs.
https://t.co/XB8ZBsntZB

Yes! Agents can evolve with their harness through RL! 🚀

Better yet, agents can learn when and how to use their harness, rather than relying on hand-crafted rules.

Smarter agents don’t need more scaffolding. They learn when to use less. 🧠

📄 https://t.co/zZGZqwfWah https://t.co/2j0RcZyZkM

Dex-One2Many gets dexterous manipulation from a single human video - not by imitating the trajectory, but by abstracting it into sequential scene graphs and letting RL fill in the motion. 94.6-96.8% on unseen configs in sim. (Oct 8)

https://t.co/b6frnjFnCq

Agents that learn in 4 rounds instead of millions of RL steps.

AgentGarten: simulators keep the world state, a distilled video model renders what the agent sees, and each round's lessons become a playbook the next agent inherits.
